title: NUMA-stable slab allocator and session snapshots to stabilize continuous enqueue
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Refactor the continuous enqueue path and the in-process KV backing allocator to adopt a compact slab allocator with explicit NUMA affinity and lightweight on-disk session snapshots. This reduces long-tail latency from GC-like pauses during heavy enqueue bursts and improves cold-start warmup for long-running chat sessions. The work replaces an ad-hoc mmap+malloc mix with a predictable slab layout, adds allocator throttling hooks for admission control, and implements a small snapshot format to checkpoint session KV state for faster recovery and prewarming.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end P95 tail latency under sustained enqueue bursts (1000 concurrent short sessions) improves by >=25% vs baseline on large-instance NUMA nodes
Allocator produces deterministic memory maps per NUMA zone and avoids cross-node migrations detected by perf tools
Session snapshot write/read cycle completes within 25ms for typical ~64KB session payloads
No higher-than-baseline OOM events in staging with 48-hour soak
Automated unit + integration tests for slab allocation, eviction, and snapshot compatibility included in PR
tasks: Design slab allocator layout and expose NUMA hinting API
Implement allocator throttling token bucket and admission hook into continuous enqueue controller
Replace existing mmap backing for hot KV segments with slab arenas per NUMA zone
Implement compact session snapshot format (versioned) and disk write path with background flush
Add prewarm path that reads snapshots into allocator arenas during model swap
Add telemetry: per-NUMA allocation counters, migratory page alerts, snapshot latencies
Create integration tests and multi-NUMA CI job to validate behavior
Performance runbooks and canary rollout configuration
benchmarks: Baseline (staging, r5g.8xlarge equiv): tail P95 during 10m sustained enqueue storm: 312ms
Target after changes: tail P95 during same test: <=234ms (>=25% improvement)
Snapshot write latency baseline: 78ms (varies with fsync), target: <=25ms using batched flush
Resident set churn metric baseline: 12 GB/hour due to page migrations, target: <2 GB/hour
testing_plan: Unit tests for slab allocation and free-list invariants
Integration job: multi-NUMA VM with synthetic enqueue generator (10m soak), validate no migratory pages and stable latencies
Chaos test: adversarial snapshot writes concurrent with heavy enqueue to validate background flush correctness
Upgrade compatibility tests: ensure newer snapshot version falls back to full replay when mismatched
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag disabled by default
2) Canary on internal infra with runtime-1.22-canary for select low-risk tenants for 48h
3) Gradual ramp to 10%/25%/100% using console rollout controller and automatic rollback if P95 regresses >10%
4) Monitor per-NUMA telemetry and migratory-page alerts for 72h post-full-rollout
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: slab allocator bug could leak or corrupt KV slots - Mitigation: extensive unit tests + ASAN builds and a memory-safe fallback path
Risk: snapshot format incompatibility with older private deployments - Mitigation: versioned snapshots + graceful fallback to replay path
Risk: changes increase write amplification on certain filesystems - Mitigation: use batched/coalesced flush and add FS-specific knobs
Risk: NUMA affinity hints not respected in some cloud VM flavors - Mitigation: runtime detects lack of NUMA and falls back to single-arena mode
